ca_2_gully_left_side.blurb: This is a small trad wall on the Donner Summit side of the I-80 corridor near Lake Tahoe, forming one half of a gully beneath the main wall. It has eight routes, nearly all of them gear climbs plus a top-rope or two, on granodiorite. Grades start around 5.6 and run up to a single 5.11, with a cluster at 5.10. The lowest-graded line is the one most climbers come for, and the harder crack and corner lines make a short day for someone working through the 5.10 range. Expect pitches of modest length that need a standard rack.

ca_attila_the_hun_wall.blurb: A compact wall in the Central Gorge of the Owens River Gorge, outside Bishop in the Eastern Sierra. It sits across the river from Faulty Towers and mixes bolted lines with a pair of crack climbs. There are eight routes in all: six sport and two trad. Grades begin at 5.7, with a handful at 5.9, a couple at 5.10 and two at 5.11, so it suits a party that wants moderates alongside a few harder pitches. The routes are short, which makes it easy to fold into a longer day of gorge climbing.

ca_snickers_south_face_left.blurb: This is a box canyon partway along the large Snickers formation in the Echo Rock area of central Joshua Tree National Park. The enclosed pocket gives some relief on windy days. Eight routes climb the monzogranite walls: seven trad lines and one aid route at A2. Free grades start at 5.8, with several at 5.10 and 5.11 and the hardest at 5.12, so it leans toward experienced leaders. One of the harder lines goes on for two pitches. Reaching the base takes a short walk on a trail followed by some scrambling.

ca_arizona_tower.blurb: Arizona Tower is a narrow fin of patina-covered rock in the southern part of the Alabama Hills near Lone Pine, set a few hundred yards from the road and just beyond Alabama Dome. The walk in follows a dirt road, and the formation is visible once you pass the cattle guard. There are eight routes, seven bolted and one on gear, ranging from 5.6 up to 5.10. Most sit between 5.7 and 5.9, so it is a good stop for moderate leaders, with one harder bolted line for a step up.

ca_tiny_dancer_wall.blurb: A small face in the Sheep Pass area of central Joshua Tree National Park, directly behind Group Campsite 3. The wall holds a range of easy cracks and face lines, eight trad routes in total. Most grades fall between 5.5 and 5.7, with a couple of climbs at 5.9 and 5.10, including routes that can also be top-roped. The walk from the campsite is only a few steps, making it a handy spot for beginners practising gear placements or for a quick warm-up. Several of the routes are short, around the 35-foot mark.

ca_camelot_castle.blurb: Camelot Castle is the first of the formations you reach in the Monty Python Castles section of the Pie Shop area, on the South Shore of Lake Tahoe. All eight routes are bolted. The grades run from 5.4 to 5.11, with the easier lines on the left and the 5.11s at the upper end, and one route is a two-pitch outing. Reaching the base means crossing a sandy wash, which lands you under the first couple of climbs. It is useful for a mixed party of beginners and stronger climbers.
